Issued at 215 PM CST Fri Nov 13 2026

An omega blocking pattern over the central CONUS continues to 
promote dry and mild conditions across western and central North
Dakota today. Moderate low level saturation is expected to 
allow at least patchy cloud cover over portions of the southwest
and south central through the day today. Have opted to slightly
lower high temperatures here due to the prevailing cloud cover,
though strong southerly surface winds will still raise 
temperatures into the 40s. With clear skies across much of 
central North Dakota, have opted to blend in (1:1 ratio) some 
NBM 90th to bump up temperatures here. The resulting picture is 
of highs in the upper 30s east to the upper 40s to to lower 50s 
west. Breezy south to southeast winds, sustained around 20 to 25
MPH and gusting as high as 40 MPH in the southwest, is expected
to develop late this morning and persist through much of the 
day as a 850mb jet slides across the region, and as the surface 
pressure gradient tightens between a surface high over northern
Minnesota, and as lee cyclogenesis over the northern Rockies 
spits out of low center into central Montana. Lingering low 
level saturation across the southwest overnight tonight may 
allow another round of fog to develop as advertised by the odd 
short term CAM, though this potential is a little more limited 
as gusty linger overnight. Thus any fog that does develop is 
expected to be fairly patchy, and more limited to where the 
stratus deck scrapes more elevated terrain. With increased cloud
cover overnight, low temperatures are forecast to remain in the
20s to lower 30s. 

Mild conditions continue through the weekend as the Omega Block
is slowly ejected eastward ahead of a pacific northwestern 
trough/opening low. High temperatures warm from the 40s to lower
50s on Saturday broadly into the 50s by Sunday as flow aloft 
becomes increasingly southwesterly. With the increasingly dry 
air streaming in across the region, low level stratus across 
much of the area Saturday morning will gradually diminish from 
southwest to northeast through Saturday evening into early 
Sunday, leaning mostly sunny conditions for Sunday afternoon. 
Breezy south to southeast winds, with sustained speeds up to 25 
to 30 MPH and gusts up to 40 MPH, are broadly expected across 
the area on Saturday as a tight pressure gradient remains draped
across the northern Plains. As this gradient is displaced 
further east, breezy south winds will linger south central North
Dakota Sunday afternoon, with winds become relatively light 
(gusting as high as 15 to 20 MPH) across the west and north 
central. 

Looking ahead, southwesterly flow over the northern Plains is 
expected to persist through the mid week and will continue to 
promote mild and dry conditions through at least Wednesday. High
temperatures through this period will linger broadly in the 
50s, while overnight lows are forecast in the 30s. Starting 
Wednesday, low to medium chances (30 to 60 percent) for 
precipitation begins to build in across the region as the 
ensemble advertises another broad Pacific Trough/closed off low 
crossing the Rockies into the northern Plains. There remains a 
large amount of discord between ensemble members on outcomes 
through this period, depending on the relative track of the 
potential low as it passes through the region. Cluster analysis 
reveals three scenarios at this time. The first (approximately 
45 percent of members) favors fairly dry conditions through the 
later half of the week as the upper level trough/low passes 
further to the north and west of the forecast area. Some limited
wrap-around light precpitation will be possible, especially 
across the northwest, but overall QPF would be limited (less 
than 0.10") in this scenario, and little to no snow accumulation
would be anticipated. Scenario 2 (approximately 35 percent of 
ensemble members) would be slightly cooler and wetter, with an 
open wave passing along a much more southerly track across the 
region, allowing for more QPF (approaching 0.25-0.5" in total 
through the weekend). While some light snow accumulations can be
anticipated across the west in this scenario, warm day-time 
temperatures with highs well into the 40s will limit and 
potential winter-weather impacts. Scenario 3 (approximately 20 
percent of members) would be the most impactful of the three 
solutions, will a slow-moving closed off upper level low 
tracking across the northern Plains. Residence time of this 
system would promote the highest potential QPF overall 
(approaching 0.5-0.75"). With this system ingesting much more 
cool air out of the Canadian Prairies, limiting high 
temperatures into the 30s by Friday/Saturday, some decent 
snowfall accumulation would be possible, with a low chance for 
2+ inches of snowfall across western North Dakota through the
